questions.prompt: Which response shows active listening during a class discussion?
options: You are saying that the group should collect evidence first.
I was not following, so continue quickly.
Your idea is too long for us.
I will speak before everyone else.
questions.correctAnswer: You are saying that the group should collect evidence first.
questions.explanation: Restating a speaker's idea shows that the listener has understood the main point.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate active listening by paraphrasing a speaker's main idea.

questions.prompt: Which word is a synonym of cautious?
options: careful
careless
noisy
late
questions.correctAnswer: careful
questions.explanation: Cautious means careful, especially when avoiding risk or mistakes.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify synonyms for grade-level vocabulary in context.

questions.prompt: Which word is the antonym of expand?
options: shrink
increase
stretch
widen
questions.correctAnswer: shrink
questions.explanation: Expand means become larger, while shrink means become smaller.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify antonyms for common academic vocabulary.

questions.prompt: Which word is an abstract noun in the sentence Courage helped the team finish the task?
options: Courage
team
task
finish
questions.correctAnswer: Courage
questions.explanation: Courage names a quality or idea that cannot be touched.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise abstract nouns in familiar sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a proper noun correctly?
options: Our class visited Kisumu during the holiday.
Our class visited city during the holiday.
Our class visited county during the holiday.
Our class visited lake during the holiday.
questions.correctAnswer: Our class visited Kisumu during the holiday.
questions.explanation: Kisumu is the name of a specific place, so it is a proper noun.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify proper nouns and use capital letters correctly.

questions.prompt: What is the plural form of criterion?
options: criteria
criterions
criterionies
criterias
questions.correctAnswer: criteria
questions.explanation: Criteria is the standard plural form of criterion.
questions.learningOutcome: Use selected irregular plural nouns correctly.

questions.prompt: Which word is an adverb in the sentence The speaker explained the point clearly?
options: clearly
speaker
explained
point
questions.correctAnswer: clearly
questions.explanation: Clearly tells how the speaker explained the point.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify adverbs that describe how actions are done.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the simple future tense?
options: We shall present our poem tomorrow.
We presented our poem yesterday.
We are presenting our poem now.
We present our poem every Friday.
questions.correctAnswer: We shall present our poem tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Shall present shows an action that will happen later.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise future tense in familiar sentences.

questions.prompt: Which punctuation mark should end the sentence How did the debate begin?
options: question mark
full stop
comma
apostrophe
questions.correctAnswer: question mark
questions.explanation: A direct question should end with a question mark.
questions.learningOutcome: Use question marks to punctuate direct questions.

questions.prompt: Which option is a complete sentence?
options: The learners revised before the assessment.
Because the learners
After revising the
Before the assessment and
questions.correctAnswer: The learners revised before the assessment.
questions.explanation: A complete sentence has a subject, a verb, and a complete idea.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify complete sentences and fragments.

questions.prompt: Which phrase is most suitable for politely interrupting a speaker?
options: Excuse me, may I add a point?
Stop talking now.
Move away from the front.
Your point is not useful.
questions.correctAnswer: Excuse me, may I add a point?
questions.explanation: The phrase uses respectful language and asks for permission before speaking.
questions.learningOutcome: Use polite expressions to take turns in discussion.

questions.prompt: Which title best fits a paragraph about borrowing books, reading daily, and returning books on time?
options: Responsible Library Use
A Broken Window
A Rainy Football Match
The Empty Basket
questions.correctAnswer: Responsible Library Use
questions.explanation: All the details describe good habits when using a library.
questions.learningOutcome: Select a suitable title from the main idea of a short text.

questions.prompt: Which word has the prefix mis- meaning wrongly?
options: misplace
teacher
kindly
return
questions.correctAnswer: misplace
questions.explanation: Misplace means to put something in the wrong place.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise common prefixes and their meanings.

questions.prompt: Which word is formed correctly using the suffix -ment?
options: development
developful
developly
developness
questions.correctAnswer: development
questions.explanation: Development is formed from develop and the suffix -ment.
questions.learningOutcome: Form nouns using common suffixes.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a formal greeting for a school assembly?
options: Good morning, teachers and fellow learners.
Hey people, listen here.
You all should keep quiet now.
What is up, everyone?
questions.correctAnswer: Good morning, teachers and fellow learners.
questions.explanation: A formal greeting is respectful and suitable for an assembly.
questions.learningOutcome: Use formal language in school oral presentations.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: The list of debate topics ___ on the noticeboard.
options: is
are
were
have
questions.correctAnswer: is
questions.explanation: The subject list is singular, so it takes the singular verb is.
questions.learningOutcome: Use verbs that agree with singular subjects followed by phrases.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the present perfect tense correctly?
options: The club has completed the project.
The club completes the project yesterday.
The club completed tomorrow.
The club is complete the project.
questions.correctAnswer: The club has completed the project.
questions.explanation: Has completed shows an action finished before now with present importance.
questions.learningOutcome: Use present perfect tense in meaningful contexts.

questions.prompt: Which word best joins the sentence We practised daily ___ we could present confidently?
options: so that
unless
although
or
questions.correctAnswer: so that
questions.explanation: So that introduces the purpose of practising daily.
questions.learningOutcome: Use conjunctions to show purpose in sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly to show ownership by several learners?
options: The learners' projects were displayed.
The learner's projects were displayed.
The learners projects' were displayed.
The learnerss' projects were displayed.
questions.correctAnswer: The learners' projects were displayed.
questions.explanation: Learners' shows that the projects belong to more than one learner.
questions.learningOutcome: Use apostrophes to show plural possession.

questions.prompt: Which word completes the sentence The team shared ___ ideas before writing the report?
options: their
there
they're
them
questions.correctAnswer: their
questions.explanation: Their shows that the ideas belonged to the team members.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose the correct homophone for a sentence context.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses commas correctly in a list?
options: The report included causes, effects, examples, and recommendations.
The report included, causes effects examples and recommendations.
The report included causes effects, examples and, recommendations.
The report included causes, effects examples, and recommendations.
questions.correctAnswer: The report included causes, effects, examples, and recommendations.
questions.explanation: Commas separate items in a list so the meaning is clear.
questions.learningOutcome: Use commas to separate items in a series.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a modal verb to show obligation?
options: Learners must submit the assignment on Friday.
Learners submitted the assignment on Friday.
Learners are submitting the assignment.
Learners submit the assignment often.
questions.correctAnswer: Learners must submit the assignment on Friday.
questions.explanation: Must is a modal verb that shows obligation or necessity.
questions.learningOutcome: Use modal verbs to express obligation and advice.

questions.prompt: Which word best completes the sentence The chairperson sat ___ the secretary and the treasurer?
options: between
among
inside
above
questions.correctAnswer: between
questions.explanation: Between is used when referring to a position involving two other people or things.
questions.learningOutcome: Use prepositions accurately in sentence contexts.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a relative pronoun correctly?
options: The learner who chaired the meeting spoke clearly.
The learner where chaired the meeting spoke clearly.
The learner when chaired the meeting spoke clearly.
The learner what chaired the meeting spoke clearly.
questions.correctAnswer: The learner who chaired the meeting spoke clearly.
questions.explanation: Who refers to a person and connects the extra information to learner.
questions.learningOutcome: Use relative pronouns to join related ideas.

questions.prompt: Which option best reports Amina said, 'I am preparing a speech'?
options: Amina said that she was preparing a speech.
Amina said that I am preparing a speech.
Amina says that she was prepared a speech.
Amina prepared that said a speech.
questions.correctAnswer: Amina said that she was preparing a speech.
questions.explanation: Reported speech changes I to she and am preparing to was preparing.
questions.learningOutcome: Change simple direct speech into reported speech.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is written in passive voice?
options: The poem was recited by the class prefect.
The class prefect recited the poem.
The class prefect is reciting loudly.
The poem sounded interesting.
questions.correctAnswer: The poem was recited by the class prefect.
questions.explanation: In passive voice, the subject receives the action.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise passive voice in simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Read: The crowd clapped as the speaker walked back to her seat. What can you infer?
options: The audience appreciated the speech.
The audience had left the hall.
The speaker forgot every word.
The hall was completely empty.
questions.correctAnswer: The audience appreciated the speech.
questions.explanation: Clapping is a clue that the audience approved of or enjoyed the speech.
questions.learningOutcome: Make simple inferences from clues in a short text.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the comparative form correctly?
options: This summary is clearer than the first draft.
This summary is clearest than the first draft.
This summary is more clearer than the first draft.
This summary clear than the first draft.
questions.correctAnswer: This summary is clearer than the first draft.
questions.explanation: Clearer is the correct comparative form for comparing two summaries.
questions.learningOutcome: Use comparative adjectives correctly in context.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the superlative form correctly?
options: Mercy gave the most convincing reason.
Mercy gave the more convincing reason of all.
Mercy gave the convincingest reason.
Mercy gave more most convincing reason.
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy gave the most convincing reason.
questions.explanation: Most convincing is the correct superlative form for this adjective.
questions.learningOutcome: Use superlative adjectives correctly in context.

questions.prompt: Which option gives the best topic sentence for details about saving water, fixing leaks, and harvesting rainwater?
options: Schools can conserve water in several practical ways.
A school gate is usually strong.
Some learners enjoy drawing maps.
The bell rang after lunch.
questions.correctAnswer: Schools can conserve water in several practical ways.
questions.explanation: The sentence introduces the shared idea behind all the supporting details.
questions.learningOutcome: Write topic sentences that match supporting details.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a transition word to show contrast?
options: The route was longer; however, it was safer.
The route was longer; therefore, we arrived.
The route was longer; next, we packed.
The route was longer; for example, a book.
questions.correctAnswer: The route was longer; however, it was safer.
questions.explanation: However signals a contrast between a longer route and a safer route.
questions.learningOutcome: Use transition words to connect contrasting ideas.

questions.prompt: Which question would be most useful when interviewing a school librarian?
options: How do you encourage learners to read more books?
Is the floor made of cement?
Can you say the word yes?
What colour is the nearest wall?
questions.correctAnswer: How do you encourage learners to read more books?
questions.explanation: The question is open-ended and directly relates to the librarian's role.
questions.learningOutcome: Ask relevant open-ended interview questions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses direct speech punctuation most clearly?
options: Njeri said, 'Please collect the scripts after class.'
Njeri said 'Please collect, the scripts after class'.
Njeri said Please, collect the scripts after class.
Njeri, said please collect the scripts after class.
questions.correctAnswer: Njeri said, 'Please collect the scripts after class.'
questions.explanation: The comma and quotation marks show the speaker's exact words clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Punctuate simple direct speech in written sentences.

questions.prompt: Which option is the best summary of a paragraph about planting trees to provide shade, protect soil, and improve air?
options: Planting trees benefits the school environment in several ways.
Trees can sometimes be tall.
Shade appears under branches.
Soil can be brown or red.
questions.correctAnswer: Planting trees benefits the school environment in several ways.
questions.explanation: A summary should capture the central idea without listing every detail.
questions.learningOutcome: Summarise the main idea of a short informational text.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has the clearest subject and predicate?
options: The drama club rehearsed after lunch.
After lunch near the hall.
The drama club and the stage.
Because the drama club.
questions.correctAnswer: The drama club rehearsed after lunch.
questions.explanation: The sentence names who acted and what action they performed.
questions.learningOutcome: Construct complete sentences with clear subjects and predicates.

questions.prompt: Which word best completes the sentence Neither the captain nor the players ___ late?
options: were
was
is
has
questions.correctAnswer: were
questions.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, players.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply subject verb agreement with paired subjects.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an interjection appropriately?
options: Bravo, the choir performed beautifully!
Chair, the choir performed beautifully!
Because, the choir performed beautifully!
Under, the choir performed beautifully!
questions.correctAnswer: Bravo, the choir performed beautifully!
questions.explanation: Bravo expresses praise and fits the feeling in the sentence.
questions.learningOutcome: Use interjections to express suitable feelings.

questions.prompt: Which word names a person who writes poems?
options: poet
pilot
editor
merchant
questions.correctAnswer: poet
questions.explanation: A poet is a person who writes poems.
questions.learningOutcome: Use basic literary terms accurately.

questions.prompt: Which word shows the speaker's attitude in the sentence Sadly, the final match was postponed?
options: Sadly
final
match
postponed
questions.correctAnswer: Sadly
questions.explanation: Sadly shows the writer's feeling about the event.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify adverbs that show attitude or manner.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is most suitable for ending a formal vote of thanks?
options: Thank you all for your attention and support.
That is all; you can go now.
I am tired of speaking.
Everyone should clap for me.
questions.correctAnswer: Thank you all for your attention and support.
questions.explanation: The sentence is respectful and fits the purpose of a formal closing.
questions.learningOutcome: Use suitable closing remarks in formal oral presentations.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly combines these ideas: The road was muddy. The learners arrived on time.
options: Although the road was muddy, the learners arrived on time.
The road was muddy because arrived learners time.
The learners arrived on time although because road.
Muddy the road and on time arrived.
questions.correctAnswer: Although the road was muddy, the learners arrived on time.
questions.explanation: Although connects the difficulty with the unexpected result.
questions.learningOutcome: Combine related ideas using subordinating conjunctions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best changes The secretary wrote the minutes into passive voice?
options: The minutes were written by the secretary.
The secretary was written by the minutes.
The minutes wrote the secretary.
The secretary had minutes written them.
questions.correctAnswer: The minutes were written by the secretary.
questions.explanation: The passive sentence makes minutes receive the action of being written.
questions.learningOutcome: Transform active sentences into passive voice accurately.

questions.prompt: Which option best reports the question 'Did you finish the group report?'
options: The teacher asked whether we had finished the group report.
The teacher asked did we finished the group report.
The teacher asked whether did we finish the report.
The teacher asked we finish the report did.
questions.correctAnswer: The teacher asked whether we had finished the group report.
questions.explanation: A reported yes-or-no question can use whether and changes the word order.
questions.learningOutcome: Report yes-or-no questions using correct word order.

questions.prompt: Read: The speaker lowered her voice and paused before the final sentence. What was she likely creating?
options: suspense
spelling
a list
a greeting
questions.correctAnswer: suspense
questions.explanation: A lowered voice and pause can make the audience wait for what comes next.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret how voice control affects meaning in oral narration.

questions.prompt: Which sentence gives the strongest evidence that a character is generous?
options: She shared her only pen with a classmate who had none.
She counted the desks in the room.
She closed the window after break.
She wrote her name on the cover.
questions.correctAnswer: She shared her only pen with a classmate who had none.
questions.explanation: Sharing something useful with someone in need shows generosity.
questions.learningOutcome: Use textual evidence to infer a character trait.

questions.prompt: Which option best explains the idiom break the ice in a meeting?
options: make people feel relaxed enough to begin talking
damage frozen water with a stone
end a discussion immediately
hide from other speakers
questions.correctAnswer: make people feel relaxed enough to begin talking
questions.explanation: To break the ice means to reduce tension at the start of a conversation.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret common idioms from context.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best uses a colon to introduce a list?
options: Bring three items: a notebook, a ruler, and a pencil.
Bring: three items a notebook, ruler and pencil.
Bring three items a notebook: a ruler and pencil.
Bring three: items: a notebook: ruler.
questions.correctAnswer: Bring three items: a notebook, a ruler, and a pencil.
questions.explanation: A colon can introduce a list after a complete opening clause.
questions.learningOutcome: Use colons to introduce lists in sentences.

questions.prompt: Which option is the best thesis statement for an essay about reading clubs?
options: Reading clubs improve vocabulary, confidence, and teamwork.
A reading club may meet on Wednesday.
Some clubs have chairs in a room.
The word reading has seven letters.
questions.correctAnswer: Reading clubs improve vocabulary, confidence, and teamwork.
questions.explanation: A thesis statement gives a clear main claim that can be supported with reasons.
questions.learningOutcome: Write clear thesis statements for opinion essays.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best supports the claim that teamwork improves learning?
options: Group members can explain difficult ideas to one another.
The group sat near a window.
Some learners wear blue sweaters.
A classroom has a door.
questions.correctAnswer: Group members can explain difficult ideas to one another.
questions.explanation: The sentence gives a reason that directly supports the claim.
questions.learningOutcome: Select relevant evidence to support a claim.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best maintains a formal tone in an email to the head teacher?
options: I kindly request permission for our club to use the hall.
Give us the hall because we need it.
Hey, we want the hall now.
The hall is ours today, okay?
questions.correctAnswer: I kindly request permission for our club to use the hall.
questions.explanation: The sentence is polite, clear, and suitable for a formal email.
questions.learningOutcome: Use formal register in emails and requests.

questions.prompt: Which detail would be most useful in a notice about a debate club meeting?
options: the date, time, venue, and agenda
the colour of the chalk
the number of trees near school
the favourite foods of members
questions.correctAnswer: the date, time, venue, and agenda
questions.explanation: A notice should give the information people need to attend and prepare.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify key details needed in notices.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best combines these notes into a report sentence: rain damaged path - learners used another gate?
options: Because rain damaged the path, learners used another gate.
Rain damaged path learners gate another because used.
Learners rain gate damaged because another path.
Another gate damaged learners because rain path.
questions.correctAnswer: Because rain damaged the path, learners used another gate.
questions.explanation: The sentence clearly links the cause with the action taken.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop notes into clear report sentences.

questions.prompt: Which question helps a reader identify the main idea of a passage?
options: What is the passage mostly about?
How many commas are in the passage?
What is the first letter of the title?
Is the paper white?
questions.correctAnswer: What is the passage mostly about?
questions.explanation: The main idea is the central point or focus of a passage.
questions.learningOutcome: Use guiding questions to identify main ideas.

questions.prompt: Which option best shows skimming?
options: reading headings and first sentences quickly to get the general idea
reading every word slowly to copy punctuation
looking for one phone number only
checking the spelling of a single word
questions.correctAnswer: reading headings and first sentences quickly to get the general idea
questions.explanation: Skimming is fast reading for the overall meaning of a text.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish skimming from other reading strategies.

questions.prompt: Which option best shows scanning?
options: looking quickly through a timetable to find the English lesson time
reading a story slowly for enjoyment
retelling all events in a novel
writing a new ending for a poem
questions.correctAnswer: looking quickly through a timetable to find the English lesson time
questions.explanation: Scanning means searching a text quickly for specific information.
questions.learningOutcome: Use scanning to locate specific information in texts.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best describes the mood in The empty field lay silent under grey clouds?
options: gloomy
playful
excited
angry
questions.correctAnswer: gloomy
questions.explanation: Empty, silent, and grey clouds create a sad or gloomy feeling.
questions.learningOutcome: Infer mood from descriptive details in a text.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best corrects the pronoun problem in When Linet met Asha, she was carrying the poster?
options: When Linet met Asha, Linet was carrying the poster.
When Linet met Asha, she and her carried it.
When she met her, the poster was carrying.
The poster met Linet and Asha.
questions.correctAnswer: When Linet met Asha, Linet was carrying the poster.
questions.explanation: Repeating Linet removes the unclear pronoun reference.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise unclear pronoun references for clear meaning.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses parallel structure correctly?
options: The project involved planning, drawing, and presenting.
The project involved planning, to draw, and presentation.
The project involved to plan, drawing, and present.
The project involved plan, drew, and presenting.
questions.correctAnswer: The project involved planning, drawing, and presenting.
questions.explanation: Planning, drawing, and presenting follow the same grammatical pattern.
questions.learningOutcome: Use parallel structure in lists and connected ideas.

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains a dependent clause?
options: Because the bell rang, the learners entered class.
The bell rang loudly.
Learners entered class quickly.
The lesson began at noon.
questions.correctAnswer: Because the bell rang, the learners entered class.
questions.explanation: Because the bell rang is a dependent clause joined to a main clause.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify dependent clauses in complex sentences.

questions.prompt: Which option best revises this run-on sentence: The bell rang we rushed to class?
options: The bell rang, and we rushed to class.
The bell rang we rushed and class.
The bell rang rushed to class we.
The bell and rushed class rang.
questions.correctAnswer: The bell rang, and we rushed to class.
questions.explanation: The revision joins two complete ideas correctly with a comma and conjunction.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise run-on sentences into clear sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence appeals most clearly to the sense of sound?
options: The drums echoed across the assembly ground.
The mango was sweet and juicy.
The paper felt rough.
The chalk looked white.
questions.correctAnswer: The drums echoed across the assembly ground.
questions.explanation: Echoed describes sound, so the sentence appeals to hearing.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sensory details in descriptive language.

questions.prompt: Which phrase uses alliteration?
options: bright blue baskets
a very tall tree
the learner wrote neatly
water flowed slowly
questions.correctAnswer: bright blue baskets
questions.explanation: Alliteration repeats the same initial consonant sound in nearby words.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise sound devices used in poems.

questions.prompt: Which line uses personification?
options: The wind whispered through the trees.
The wind moved through the trees.
The wind was cold at night.
The wind blew from the hill.
questions.correctAnswer: The wind whispered through the trees.
questions.explanation: Whispered gives the wind a human action.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify personification in literary language.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best uses a simile?
options: Her explanation was as clear as daylight.
Her explanation was clear.
Her explanation cleared the table.
Her explanation was a notebook.
questions.correctAnswer: Her explanation was as clear as daylight.
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using as or like.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify similes and explain their effect.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best uses a metaphor?
options: Books are windows to new worlds.
Books are like windows.
Books have paper pages.
Books are kept on shelves.
questions.correctAnswer: Books are windows to new worlds.
questions.explanation: A metaphor directly compares books to windows without using like or as.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify metaphors in literary and informational texts.

questions.prompt: Which option best identifies the purpose of a school report?
options: to present information about an event or activity clearly
to hide facts from readers
to list random words for practice
to entertain only through jokes
questions.correctAnswer: to present information about an event or activity clearly
questions.explanation: A report gives organised factual information about something that happened.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the purpose and features of report writing.

questions.prompt: Which option is the best order for writing a narrative?
options: orientation, problem, events, resolution
resolution, title, random facts, greeting
problem, dictionary, venue, date
events, ingredients, vote, address
questions.correctAnswer: orientation, problem, events, resolution
questions.explanation: A narrative usually introduces the setting, develops a problem, and resolves it.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan narratives with a clear sequence of events.

questions.prompt: Which sentence would work best as the opening of a story?
options: At dawn, our class bus stopped beside the quiet museum gate.
The story ended and everyone went home.
In conclusion, that is my opinion.
The notice will be pinned tomorrow.
questions.correctAnswer: At dawn, our class bus stopped beside the quiet museum gate.
questions.explanation: The sentence introduces time, setting, and action that can begin a story.
questions.learningOutcome: Create engaging openings for narratives.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best uses a cause-and-effect relationship?
options: The power went off, so the learners moved near the windows to read.
The power went off and the word power has five letters.
The learners moved because window near read.
Windows are sometimes made of glass.
questions.correctAnswer: The power went off, so the learners moved near the windows to read.
questions.explanation: The sentence shows a cause and the action that resulted from it.
questions.learningOutcome: Use connectors to show cause and effect.

questions.prompt: Which option best explains why eye contact matters in a speech?
options: It helps the speaker connect with the audience.
It changes the spelling of words.
It makes the speech shorter automatically.
It replaces the need for clear ideas.
questions.correctAnswer: It helps the speaker connect with the audience.
questions.explanation: Appropriate eye contact supports confidence and audience engagement.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of non-verbal cues in oral presentation.

questions.prompt: Which revision best improves this weak sentence: The place was nice?
options: The library was bright, quiet, and filled with neatly labelled shelves.
The place was nice and nice.
The place was there at school.
Nice was the place and it was.
questions.correctAnswer: The library was bright, quiet, and filled with neatly labelled shelves.
questions.explanation: The revision replaces a vague word with specific details.
questions.learningOutcome: Improve descriptions by using precise details.

questions.prompt: Which sentence does not belong in a paragraph about preparing for a debate?
options: The mango tree near the gate is very old.
The team researched the topic.
The speakers arranged their points.
The chairperson checked the rules.
questions.correctAnswer: The mango tree near the gate is very old.
questions.explanation: The sentence about a tree is unrelated to debate preparation.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify irrelevant sentences in a paragraph.

questions.prompt: Which paragraph is most coherent?
options: We selected a topic. We researched facts. We presented our findings.
We selected a topic. My shoe is black. The moon was bright.
Research is useful. I like mangoes. The gate was locked.
The topic was selected. Tables have legs. Rain is wet.
questions.correctAnswer: We selected a topic. We researched facts. We presented our findings.
questions.explanation: All the sentences stay on one topic and follow a logical order.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate coherence in short paragraphs.

questions.prompt: Which statement best evaluates the claim Every learner in Kenya loves poetry?
options: It is too broad because it cannot be proved for every learner.
It is strong because it names Kenya.
It is a fact because it uses the word every.
It is a command because it mentions poetry.
questions.correctAnswer: It is too broad because it cannot be proved for every learner.
questions.explanation: A strong claim should be reasonable and possible to support with evidence.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate claims for clarity and support.

questions.prompt: Which evidence best supports the claim that reading improves vocabulary?
options: Learners meet new words in stories and learn their meanings from context.
Some storybooks have colourful covers.
A book can be placed on a desk.
The library opens at eight o'clock.
questions.correctAnswer: Learners meet new words in stories and learn their meanings from context.
questions.explanation: The evidence directly explains how reading can build vocabulary.
questions.learningOutcome: Select relevant evidence to support reading claims.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best changes the tone from informal to formal?
options: Kindly submit the completed forms by Friday.
Hand in those forms quickly, people.
You must bring the forms or else.
Forms, forms, bring them now.
questions.correctAnswer: Kindly submit the completed forms by Friday.
questions.explanation: The sentence is polite, specific, and suitable for formal communication.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise informal language into formal register.

questions.prompt: Which option best explains the effect of repeating the line We shall try again in a poem?
options: It emphasises determination and gives the poem rhythm.
It proves the poem has no meaning.
It changes every noun into a verb.
It removes the speaker from the poem.
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasises determination and gives the poem rhythm.
questions.explanation: Repetition can stress an idea and create a memorable rhythm.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the effect of repetition in poems.

questions.prompt: Which question best helps analyse a character's motive?
options: Why did the character hide the lost note from the group?
What colour was the note?
How many letters are in the character's name?
Was the classroom door open?
questions.correctAnswer: Why did the character hide the lost note from the group?
questions.explanation: A motive question asks why a character acted in a certain way.
questions.learningOutcome: Ask analytical questions about character motivation.

questions.prompt: Which option best identifies problem-and-solution text structure?
options: The writer explains litter in the compound, then gives ways to reduce it.
The writer lists days of the week in order.
The writer describes the colour of one classroom wall.
The writer names characters in a play without events.
questions.correctAnswer: The writer explains litter in the compound, then gives ways to reduce it.
questions.explanation: Problem-and-solution structure presents an issue and possible ways to fix it.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify problem-and-solution structure in informational texts.

questions.prompt: Which option best compares two poems?
options: Both poems describe courage, but the first uses a hopeful tone while the second is sad.
The first poem has words, and the second poem also has words.
Both poems are printed on pages.
The poems have titles at the top.
questions.correctAnswer: Both poems describe courage, but the first uses a hopeful tone while the second is sad.
questions.explanation: A useful comparison explains an important similarity and difference.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare themes and tone across short literary texts.

questions.prompt: Which revision best fixes the misplaced modifier in Carrying a camera, the museum gate impressed us?
options: Carrying a camera, we were impressed by the museum gate.
Carrying a camera, the museum gate impressed us.
The museum gate carried a camera and impressed us.
Impressed us carrying a camera, the museum gate.
questions.correctAnswer: Carrying a camera, we were impressed by the museum gate.
questions.explanation: The revision makes it clear that we, not the gate, carried the camera.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise misplaced modifiers for clear meaning.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best joins a concession and a result?
options: Although the poem was difficult, the group discussed it and understood the message.
The poem difficult although because group message.
The group understood and although the difficult.
The poem was a poem, and difficult was difficult.
questions.correctAnswer: Although the poem was difficult, the group discussed it and understood the message.
questions.explanation: The sentence shows a challenge, an action, and the result clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Create complex sentences that connect contrast and result.

questions.prompt: Which response best shows respectful disagreement in a debate?
options: I understand your point, but the evidence suggests a different view.
That point is useless and wrong.
You should stop speaking now.
My view matters and yours does not.
questions.correctAnswer: I understand your point, but the evidence suggests a different view.
questions.explanation: Respectful disagreement recognises the other speaker before giving a reasoned response.
questions.learningOutcome: Disagree respectfully while supporting a viewpoint.

questions.prompt: Which option best evaluates the speaker's delivery if she mumbles, faces the board, and avoids pauses?
options: She should improve voice projection, audience contact, and pacing.
She should only change the colour of her notebook.
She has already used perfect delivery.
She should remove all examples from the speech.
questions.correctAnswer: She should improve voice projection, audience contact, and pacing.
questions.explanation: Clear voice, audience contact, and controlled pace help listeners follow a speech.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate delivery techniques in oral presentations.

questions.prompt: Which option best turns these notes into a clear notice heading: debate club - practice - Friday?
options: Debate Club Practice on Friday
Friday and club because debate
Practice notice heading maybe
Club debate practice Friday because
questions.correctAnswer: Debate Club Practice on Friday
questions.explanation: The heading names the activity and time clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Create clear headings for notices.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best uses a semicolon between related independent clauses?
options: The rain stopped; the match resumed immediately.
The rain stopped; because the match.
The rain; stopped the match resumed.
The; rain stopped, the match.
questions.correctAnswer: The rain stopped; the match resumed immediately.
questions.explanation: A semicolon can join closely related complete sentences.
questions.learningOutcome: Use semicolons to connect related independent clauses.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best changes this weak instruction into a clear one: Do the thing there?
options: Place the completed charts on the front table before break.
Do thing there quickly maybe.
The thing should be done somewhere.
There is a thing for doing.
questions.correctAnswer: Place the completed charts on the front table before break.
questions.explanation: The revision states the action, object, place, and time clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Make instructions clear, specific, and complete.

questions.prompt: Which option best identifies bias in a statement?
options: It presents one side unfairly and ignores other reasonable views.
It gives the date of an event.
It defines a word from the dictionary.
It lists the members of a club.
questions.correctAnswer: It presents one side unfairly and ignores other reasonable views.
questions.explanation: Bias happens when information favours one side unfairly.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise bias in simple texts and statements.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best uses context clues for the word scarce?
options: Water was scarce after the long dry season, so each class used only one bucket.
Water was scarce and everyone had many full tanks.
Water was scarce because the classroom was noisy.
Water was scarce, which means the bell rang early.
questions.correctAnswer: Water was scarce after the long dry season, so each class used only one bucket.
questions.explanation: The clue about limited water use shows that scarce means not enough or hard to find.
questions.learningOutcome: Use context clues to infer meanings of unfamiliar words.

questions.prompt: Which option is the best conclusion for a paragraph about keeping the school compound clean?
options: For these reasons, every learner should help keep the compound tidy.
The library has new curtains.
A pencil can be sharpened before class.
Some roads become dusty in January.
questions.correctAnswer: For these reasons, every learner should help keep the compound tidy.
questions.explanation: The conclusion restates the paragraph's main idea and gives closure.
questions.learningOutcome: Write conclusions that match paragraph ideas.

questions.prompt: Which outline best fits an argumentative essay supporting school gardens?
options: Claim, reason on food, reason on teamwork, counterpoint, conclusion
Greeting, recipe, football score, shopping list, signature
Title, random facts, joke, map, proverb
Problem, poem, timetable, address, song
questions.correctAnswer: Claim, reason on food, reason on teamwork, counterpoint, conclusion
questions.explanation: An argumentative outline should state a claim, support it, address another view, and conclude.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan argumentative essays with claims, reasons, and conclusions.

questions.prompt: Which option best synthesises two texts, one about reading clubs and one about library access?
options: Both texts show that learners read more when schools provide books and supportive groups.
Both texts use full stops at the end of some sentences.
One text has a title and the other has paragraphs.
Both texts are made of English words.
questions.correctAnswer: Both texts show that learners read more when schools provide books and supportive groups.
questions.explanation: Synthesis combines important ideas from more than one text into a broader understanding.
questions.learningOutcome: Combine ideas from related texts to form a clear conclusion.

questions.prompt: Which revision best improves cohesion in this pair: We planted trees. The shade helped learners read outside?
options: We planted trees; as a result, the shade helped learners read outside.
We planted trees shade helped because outside learners.
Trees were planted and shade and learners and outside.
The shade helped because planted trees outside read.
questions.correctAnswer: We planted trees; as a result, the shade helped learners read outside.
questions.explanation: As a result clearly links the action to its effect.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise sentences to show logical relationships between ideas.

questions.prompt: Which question best evaluates the credibility of an online article used for homework?
options: Who wrote it, when was it published, and what evidence does it give?
Does it have the longest title in the search results?
Are there many bright colours on the page?
Can I copy the first sentence quickly?
questions.correctAnswer: Who wrote it, when was it published, and what evidence does it give?
questions.explanation: Credibility depends on authorship, currency, evidence, and reliability.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate simple sources for reliability and usefulness.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best creates suspense in a narrative?
options: Just as I reached for the envelope, footsteps sounded behind the door.
The envelope was rectangular and made of paper.
I wrote my name at the top of the page.
The story ended before lunch.
questions.correctAnswer: Just as I reached for the envelope, footsteps sounded behind the door.
questions.explanation: The sentence delays the outcome and introduces a sudden sound, creating suspense.
questions.learningOutcome: Create suspense through pacing and detail in narratives.

questions.prompt: Which option best evaluates this summary: The passage talks about things?
options: It is too vague because it does not name the main idea or key details.
It is strong because it is very short.
It is accurate because every passage has things.
It is formal because it has five words.
questions.correctAnswer: It is too vague because it does not name the main idea or key details.
questions.explanation: A useful summary should state the central idea clearly and include key points.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate summaries for clarity and completeness.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best integrates a quotation into a paragraph?
options: The narrator shows determination when she says, 'I will try again tomorrow.'
I will try again tomorrow because quotation.
The narrator says and the quote is there.
Try again tomorrow narrator determination.
questions.correctAnswer: The narrator shows determination when she says, 'I will try again tomorrow.'
questions.explanation: The sentence introduces the quotation and connects it to the idea it supports.
questions.learningOutcome: Integrate quoted evidence smoothly into written responses.

questions.prompt: Which option best explains how tone changes meaning in the sentence That was clever?
options: A warm tone can show praise, while a mocking tone can show criticism.
Tone changes the spelling of clever.
Tone removes punctuation from the sentence.
Tone makes the sentence a poem automatically.
questions.correctAnswer: A warm tone can show praise, while a mocking tone can show criticism.
questions.explanation: The same words can carry different meanings depending on the speaker's tone.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how tone affects meaning in spoken language.

questions.prompt: Which ending best resolves a story about a group that disagreed over a class project?
options: After listening to every idea, the group combined the strongest suggestions and completed the project.
The group forgot the project and counted stones.
The classroom turned into a timetable.
Everyone stopped talking, so the story had no result.
questions.correctAnswer: After listening to every idea, the group combined the strongest suggestions and completed the project.
questions.explanation: The ending resolves the disagreement through listening, cooperation, and action.
questions.learningOutcome: Create logical resolutions for narratives involving conflict.

questions.prompt: Which title best fits a poem about courage, repeated effort, and hope after failure?
options: Trying Again at Dawn
The Empty Cupboard
A Roadside Sign
The Broken Stapler
questions.correctAnswer: Trying Again at Dawn
questions.explanation: The title reflects courage, renewal, and persistence after a setback.
questions.learningOutcome: Create suitable titles for poems based on central ideas.
